abstract: Clara Shih analyzes the AI-driven disruption to the labor market, highlighting a significant deterioration in entry-level employment outcomes for recent college graduates. New graduate hiring in large tech has declined over 50% since 2019, and for the first time in decades, recent college graduates face higher unemployment rates than the national average, with underemployment reaching 42.5% in Q4 2025.
keyFindings: New graduate hiring in large tech companies has declined over 50% since 2019.
Recent college graduates now have a higher unemployment rate than the national average for the first time in over a decade.
The underemployment rate for recent graduates reached 42.5% in Q4 2025, according to the New York Federal Reserve.
methodology: Analysis of hiring trends in large tech companies and labor statistics from the New York Federal Reserve (Q4 2025 data). Specific sample size and detailed analytical approach not specified.
qualifiers: Data primarily focused on large tech sector hiring; national unemployment comparisons referenced but specific comparison data not detailed. Scope appears limited to recent college graduates rather than broader labor market segments.
